observed_current_candidate.note: Immutable candidate fetch succeeded. Guard tests and static-integrity checks were skipped after the build step failed. Artifact did not preserve compiler stderr, so header absence or another exact runner cause is not inferred.

grf.observed_anchor: PR #557 calls SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED for schema main and is explicitly only a diagnostic candidate; SQLite WAL mode uses a separate WAL sqlite3_file object.
grf.generated_reality: If main-file HAS_MOVED is an adequate productive persistence-object discriminator in WAL mode, rebinding only the active WAL pathname/object should either be detected by the main-file guard or prevent the connection from continuing a successful WAL transaction.
grf.counter_reality: The main database file can remain unmoved while the already-open WAL file object is renamed/rebound independently; main-file HAS_MOVED can remain false while the same connection continues writing to its opened WAL object.
grf.falsifier: Rename the active WAL sidecar while leaving the main database object untouched, replace the visible -wal pathname with a distinct inode, then query main-file HAS_MOVED and execute a new transaction/readback on the same open connection.

unusual_experiment.name: WAL_SIDECAR_REBIND_VISIBILITY

intervention.operation: rename active FRANK_UNIFIED.sqlite-wal to FRANK_UNIFIED.original.sqlite-wal and create a distinct file at the original visible -wal pathname

limitations: Not a WAL corruption reproduction and not evidence of data loss.
Does not prove an attacker can perform this on the production deployment.
Shows a measurement-scope/object-binding gap only: main-file HAS_MOVED does not attest the WAL file object.

primary_source_alignment.sqlite_fcntl_has_moved: SQLite documents SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED as reporting whether the nominated file has been renamed, moved, or deleted since it was opened.
primary_source_alignment.sqlite_journal_pointer: SQLite documents SQLITE_FCNTL_JOURNAL_POINTER as exposing the sqlite3_file object associated with the rollback journal or write-ahead log for a database connection.
primary_source_alignment.wal_release_boundary: SQLite WAL-reset corruption issue is fixed in 3.51.3+; version suitability alone still does not prove productive object/runtime binding.

architecture_delta.delta: Productive WAL acceptance must bind both the main database object and the connection's active WAL/journal object (or prove an equivalently strong fail-closed topology) across the measured operation. Main-file HAS_MOVED alone is insufficient.
architecture_delta.smallest_next_discriminator: On the actual productive Frank connection, combine connection-bound sqlite_version/sqlite_source_id/journal_mode with object-bound main and WAL/journal identity (prefer SQLITE_FCNTL_FILE_POINTER and SQLITE_FCNTL_JOURNAL_POINTER or an equivalently strong VFS/FD-bound mechanism), execute a unique transaction/readback, then revalidate after service restart/reopen and rollback/downgrade/library-swap controls on the accepted Hostinger target.
architecture_delta.rollback: No product code changed; retain current main and keep PR #557 Draft until a WAL-aware composition is independently tested.

next_priority: Accepted Hostinger ProductStart + exact fixed SQLite runtime + real canonical UnifiedDB WAL operation + main/WAL object binding + restart/reopen + downgrade/library-swap/rollback + semantic-lineage evidence in one fail-closed provenance chain.
